text.p: Applied Graphics Technologies Inc said Tuesday it had acquired the assets of SpotLink Inc from Western International Media Corp for 539,683 AGT shares.
AGT said the acquisition will expand its digital imaging, archiving and distribution services, and give it an important presence in the broadcast market.
Based on SpotLink projections, the acquisition will be accretive to AGT earnings in 1997, the company said.
AGT said it now has 13.8 million shares outstanding.
Western International Media is a subsidiary of Interpublic Group of Cos Inc.

AGT said it is a leader in the digital distribution of content for print media, and SpotLink is a leader in the volume reproduction and distribution (dub and ship) of television and radio commercials to broadcast and cable media for advertising agencies and their clients.

AGT said Western International Media has agreed to direct its analog and digital 'dub and ship' business to AGT/SpotLink for the next 10 years. It described Western as the premier U.S. media management firm and the largest buyer of television, radio and out-of-home advertising, as well as a major buyer of print, cable, yellow pages and direct mail.

SpotLink estimates its 1996 revenues will be $6.3 million. AGT will continue to operate SpotLink's audio and video volume reproduction and distribution facilities in Wilmington, Ohio, and anticipates no layoffs as a result of the acquisition.
